Prone to Shifting and Subject to Damage 
Use extreme care when switching commodities subject to damage, especially when cars are partly loaded or unloaded. 
(E.g., shed, team, or industrial tracks) 
Service Equipment 
The following instructions apply when switching service equipment cars.   
a) Do not couple to or move “occupied” service equipment cars, unless authorized by the person in charge.  
b) Do not cut off in motion.  
c) Do not cut off other cars in motion towards these cars.  
d) Before coupling to or moving service equipment:  
1. Stop between 12 and 6 feet from the cars to be coupled or moved.  
(CAUTION: Ensure coupler heads are properly aligned.)  
2. Notify persons in or about the cars.  
3. Check cars to ensure all cables, hoses, temporary ladders etc., have been removed.  
4. After receiving the proper signal, couple carefully to avoid shock. 
 
Multi-Platform cars (Multi-Level Auto Racks are not considered Multi-Platform) 
        When loaded or empty: 
• 
Do not cut off in motion. 
• 
Do not allow to be struck by a car moving under its own momentum. 
TEC (Track Evaluation Car) 
• 
Handle with extreme care to avoid damage (Cars 63 and 64 are equipped with shock sensors.) 
• 
Do not pass over tracks with a hump or inert retarders. 
• 
Do not uncouple TEC cars and TEC locomotives without permission from TEC staff. 
• 
Handle as “occupied passenger equipment”, unless otherwise indicated. (This includes switching and train 
handling, when running light or deadheading, with or without the TEC staff aboard). 
• 
When testing, cars 63 and 64 should have the “A” end (with viewing window) trailing, unless authorized by the 
TEC staff to facilitate handling. 
Trailers or Containers 
Trailers and containers should not be cut off in motion or struck by a car moving under its own momentum. If these actions 
cannot be avoided, then ensure couplings are made at the lowest speed possible.  
Two Axle Scale Test Cars see scale test car Item 2.8 
 
2.4 Marshalling Restrictions-Equipment and Loads 
Loaded Multi-Level Autos  
Do not place loaded multi-level autos immediately behind open top cars containing coal, sand, gravel, sulphur, or similar 
commodities. 
 
Snowplows and Spreaders handled in deadhead service. 
• 
Marshall at the extreme rear of train. 
• 
Run in the direction of travel. 
• 
Do not marshall nose to nose.  
• 
See Speed Restriction Chart for restrictions while moving in train. 
• 
When handled in work service, employee in charge will determine placement of car in train. 
If not possible to run in the direction of travel: 
• 
Wings must remain properly secured. 
• 
Snow must not pack behind wings during movement. 
• 
Must be turned at first available wye or turntable. 
 
Two axle intermodal cars (Car Code QA)  
Trailing tonnage must not exceed 1,500 tons.  
 
Single Trailer on TOFC 
A single trailer on TOFC equipment with two hitches must not be loaded on the center hitch.  
 
Rear End Only 
Cars tagged, stenciled, billed as "Rear End Only" must be marshalled to the rear of the train.

Note: Train Area Marshalling messages do not indicate when trailing car tonnage exceeds this maximum.  This item also 
applies to Cabooses that have been modified for use by other departments. 
 
2.6 Bad Order 
***Bad Order*** 
A train receiving this Car Movement Restriction Message (CMRM) on any of the following documents:  
• 
Work Order, 
• 
Car Handling Report,  
• 
Outbound Wheel Report or 
• 
Tonnage Profile 
Indicates the car(s) has/have Mechanical defect(s) and subject car(s) must not be lifted or moved unless instructions are 
received from the Dispatcher that the car(s) is/are safe to travel, these instructions may or may not include Restrictions or 
Special Handling information.  In some cases, a Mechanical employee may provide the required handling instructions directly 
to the crew.  
 
In all instances, the train crew must record the handling information received, on the Crew Information form. 
 
B/O, Safe to Travel 
A train receiving this Car Movement Restriction Message (CMRM) has a Bad Order car that has been deemed safe to travel 
by Mechanical, and can/must be handled on the train, in accordance with the CMR Messages received. 
 
2.7 Loads Prone to Shifting 
Marshalling restrictions apply when lading is both in an open top car or a container in the end position on the car and not 
protected by end bulkheads extending to top of lading. Also applies to gondolas with removable end bulkheads.  
 
Loads prone to shifting include pipe, timber, poles, metal rods, rail, or other similar material on flat cars. Other similar material 
includes coil steel not covered and/or not protected by end or special bulkheads. 
Must be Marshalled as follows: 
Separate loads prone to shifting must not be placed next to: 
• 
Occupied cabooses, passenger cars or service equipment cars  
• 
Placarded tank car (subject to the Instructions for Handling Hazardous Material).  
• 
Locmotive(s). 
Separate loads prone to shifting by at least two cars of any type, or by one:  
• 
full sized steel box car, 
• 
car loaded with one or more containers, or 
• 
bulkhead type car the ends of which extend above the load being protected against. 
 
Exception: This rule does not apply to road switchers when handling bulkhead flat cars loaded with tree length wood when 
they do not have other equipment to use as cover (subject to the Instructions for Handling Hazardous Material).  
 
Note: Unit pipe trains are restricted to a maximum of 5000 feet, excluding locomotives. Non-unit pipe shipments on 
conventional trains greater than 5000 feet in length, are restricted to a maximum of 30 loads of pipe. 
 
Special Loads Requiring Observation 
Marshall as close as possible to the leading locomotive. 
Notification that a special load is in the train is given by:  
• 
train consist or protection notice.  
or  
• 
Operations Center. 
Note: These loads are not prone to shifting:  
• 
Machinery / vehicles loaded on flat cars that are equipped with special tie-down devices; 
• 
Bulkhead flats loaded with banded or packaged lumber that does not extend above the bulkhead by more than 
50 percent. 
• 
Freight car wheels loaded on special flat cars or in containers specially designed for transporting wheels. 
 
Transformers or Circuit Breakers 
Marshall at head-end of the train, no more 600 feet from the locomotive, when practicable.

Section 2 – Speed and Equipment Restrictions

Pulpwood 
Do not pull loads of pulpwood from any wood yard, unless they meet the following requirements:  
a. Loads must be level over the entire length of the car and must not extend above the end bulkheads. Loads of hardwood 
must not be loaded above the yellow line on the end of bulkheads.  
b. Loads must be properly bumped up, with no voids or open spaces within the load that will allow the load to shift.  
c. Loads must not protrude over the sides of a car more than one (1) foot.  
d. Pulpwood must be tilted toward the center of the car, and tilt maintained throughout the entire height of the load.  
 
Any cars loaded contrary to these requirements must not be pulled and the appropriate personnel notified. The conductor 
will advise the dispatcher of the car number, location, and reason for leaving the car.  The dispatcher will notify the Car 
Department, who will inspect the load and advise if and when the car can move.

-  80 cars total, and 
-  service equipment cars only.

2.11 Track Evaluation Cars (TEC)  
TEC cars: 60 / 63 / 64 / 65 / 68 / 424993 & 424994 
Equipment Description 
Air Brakes and Hand Brakes  
• 
Hand brakes are located on the vestibule ends of cars 63, 64, and 65. 
• 
Hand brakes on cars 68, 424993 and 424994 are located on the “B” end of the cars (Car 68 does not have a 
vestibule). 
• 
The instrumented truck of car 64 has a valve that applies brakes during an emergency application, but not 
during a service application. This is considered operative brakes in the application of air brake rules (Car 64 
can be Marshalled at rear of train). 
 
Additional Information  
• 
TV/Video cameras are mounted on the forward end of the dedicated locomotive to allow the TEC operators to 
see up-coming track appliances. 
• 
An intercom system located in the cab of the dedicated locomotive connects the Locomotive Engineer with the 
TEC staff when testing. 
• 
Cars 63 and 64 have a protective skirt installed over the gauge measuring beam, which extends to the top of 
the rail. This approved installation creates no risk to the movement of these cars, or to the public. 
• 
424993 is equipped with a Gauge Restraint Measurement System (GRMS).  This assembly applies the test 
loads of the measurement system to the track during a “gauge stress measurement test.”  TEC staff retract the 
assembly when not required.

•

• 
Do not pass over tracks with a hump or inert retarders. 
• 
Do not uncouple TEC cars and TEC locomotives without permission from TEC staff. 
•

handling, when running light or deadheading, with or without the TEC staff aboard).

When testing, cars 63 and 64 should have the “A” end (with viewing window) trailing, unless authorized by the 
TEC staff to facilitate handling.

Section 2 – Speed and Equipment Restrictions 
 
17 
 
Break-in-two - Cars Carrying Long Strings of Rail  
• 
Notify Train Dispatcher immediately. Give location and all pertinent information regarding break-in-two. 
• 
If possible, clear the main track before attempting to re-couple. When attempting to re-couple, ensure all rails 
enter the proper compartment on the roller racks. 
• 
If the train is on a grade, apply sufficient hand brakes to secure cars, until air pressure behind the break-in-two 
is restored. (This prevents movement if the air brakes leak off.) Where grades are involved, it is preferable to 
handle on descending grades to set off point. 
• 
If the train is on level or nearly level grade, cars of rail may be safely pulled to the nearest set-off point providing: 
o 
The movement is made using extreme caution, and 
o 
Abrupt starts and stops are avoided.   
• 
To restore air throughout the entire train and to tie cars together at the point of break-in-two, the following 
equipment is in brackets on the side of the anchor car near the center of the rail train. 
o 
Two 25-ft. and one 15-ft. air hoses with connections, 
o 
Two 25-ft. and one 15-ft. length of 1” cable with hooks. 
 
Rail Shifting  
If one or more strings of welded rail shifts: 
• 
Notify the Train Dispatcher immediately. Give location and all pertinent information. 
• 
If possible, remove anchors and loosen tie-down bolts on displaced strings. 
• 
To pull strings into place, use: 
o 
Safety pull hoists (located in the side of the roller rack on the first car behind the tie-down car), or winch on 
“threader car” (if available). 
• 
After readjusting strings and recoupling cars, re-tighten all hold-down bolts and reapply anchors. 
 
Speed Restrictions - CPKC CWR trains on CN  
The following speed restrictions apply to CPKC CWR trains operating on CN Track. 
When loaded (maximum 82 cars) with 1 or more rails, do not exceed: 
• 
40 MPH on straight track 
• 
30 MPH on curves 
• 
10 MPH through turnouts  
When empty, maximum authorized speed:  
• 
50 MPH.  
Note: Loaded CPKC CWR cars (maximum 40) may be moved in regular trains on CN Track, provided the cars (including 
buffers), are Marshalled on the Head End of the train. 
 
2.13 Air Dump Cars  
Only employees who are knowledgeable in the operation of air dump cars may operate such cars in unloading operations. 
When air dump cars are being operated, the conductor must personally supervise the handling to see that all people are in 
the clear before charging actuating airline and before they are operated.  
• 
Dump cars must not be unattended while charged.  
• 
Dumping Reservoirs must not be charged until dumping is to begin.  
• 
Dumping Reservoir must be bled off after dumping is complete.  
• 
Employees are prohibited from riding inside air dump cars.  
• 
Cars must not be moved with doors open, except as necessary to clear material just dumped. 
• 
Empty air-dump cars will be handled on rear-end of train only.  
 Protection of Adjacent Tracks: Before charging the actuating airline or before attempting to dump air dump cars, it must be 
known that protection against movement on adjacent tracks, which could be fouled by material to be dumped, has been 
provided.   
 
Air Connections between locomotive and air dump car are made as follows:  
1. Locomotive Main Reservoir Hose to Air Dump Actuating Hose: This connection provides the air supply from the locomotive 
main reservoir to the dumping reservoirs on the air dump car. The brake pipe hoses remain coupled and angle cocks cut in 
between locomotive(s) and the air dump car(s) to allow use of train air brakes while dumping. Use extreme caution when 
uncoupling the locomotive main reservoir hose from the air dump actuating hose.  
2. Locomotive Brake Pipe to Air Dump Actuating Hose:  
This connection provides the air supply from the locomotive brake pipe to the dumping reservoirs on the air dump car. This 
method is to be used only when a connection cannot be made from the locomotive main reservoir hose and the air dump 
cars actuating hose. The following will apply when using this method:  
a. Properly secure the car(s).  
b. Separate brake pipe connection between the air dump car and the locomotive.  
c. Connect locomotive brake pipe hose to the actuating hose on the air dump car.  
d. Raise brake pipe pressure on the locomotive to 120 PSI by use of the regulating valve.  
NOTE: The air dump car actuating line is at a right angle to the pipe when cut-in and parallel with the pipe when cut-out.

2.19 Severe Weather Warnings 
The following procedure will be followed in the notification of Severe Weather Warnings which includes but not limited to High

When a Severe Weather Warning, is received, the Train Dispatcher will: 
• 
Contact all trains in affected area and advise the train crews on the adverse weather condition(s). 
• 
Determine from crew or employees in field the local conditions they are observing. 
• 
Trains will then be governed by the train dispatcher instructions in the handling of their trains in line with GCOR 
6.21.  
 
If a temporary speed restriction or stopped train movement is given it will remain in effect until otherwise advised by the train 
dispatcher. 
 
Critical Areas  
Refer to your Timetable for specific critical areas listed under Severe Weather Critical Areas in the speed section. If it is not 
listed, then there would be no critical areas for that subdivision. 
 
High Wind Warnings 
Winds or Gust between 55 to 64 MPH: 
When notified of a High Wind Warning by the Train Dispatcher, all trains containing empty bulkhead cars or double stack 
intermodal traffic will be restricted to 25 MPH.

Section 3 – General Code of Operating Rules – Special Instructions 
 
19 
 
Enroute Failure  
Following a successful initialization of the PTC system, any failure or malfunction that prohibits the PTC system from operating 
as intended after the train has departed an initial terminal. When required to change lead locomotive(s) at enroute crew change 
location, the PTC system will be handled as if it were the initial terminal. No train with an inoperative PTC system may depart or 
pass a designated PTC repair facility. These locations include St. Paul, Kansas City, and Shreveport.  
 
Fouling (employee or contractor) a track  
The placement of an individual in such proximity to a track that the individual could be struck by a moving train or other on-track 
equipment, or in any case is within four feet of the nearest rail.  
 
Hard Cut In (PTC)  
A state of the PTC system when PTC cut out switches are placed in the cut in position.  
 
Hard Cut Out (PTC)  
A state of the PTC system when PTC cut out switches are placed in the cut-out position.  
 
Intermodal Trains  
Trains consisting entirely of intermodal equipment and/or automotive business. 
 
Initial Terminal 
Location where the train is originally assembled.   
 
Loaded Bulk Commodity Train  
Loaded Bulk Commodity trains are defined as a train of fifty (50) or more loaded cars in a block, each weighing 125 tons gross 
weight or more (bulk commodities), such as coal, grain, soda ash, etc.  
 
Non-controlled Track  
Track upon which trains are permitted by railroad rule or special instruction to move without receiving authorization from a train 
dispatcher or control operator.  
 
Non-enforcement State (PTC)  
A state when the PTC system is cut out, failed, degraded, disengaged, or experiencing other unenforceable conditions.  
 
Off-Track Equipment  
Machines that may be operated on the right of way foul of track.  
 
Personal electronic or electrical device   
An electronic or electrical device that was not provided to the railroad operating employee by the employing railroad for one or 
more business purposes.  
 
Power Assisted Switch (PAS)  
A switch identified as PAS can be controlled remotely by use of a DTMF keypad located on the engine radio or the 
Conductor/Brakeman Pack set. This switch can also be controlled by a push button and hand pump located at the switch in the 
event of DTMF failure.  
 
PTC System Cut Out - a soft key cut out on Engineers PTC display or cycling the horn, penalty or emergency toggle switches 
to cut out position. 
 
Quiet Zone  
A segment of rail line, within which is situated one or a number of consecutive public highway-rail crossings at which locomotive 
horns are not routinely sounded.  Signs may be used to mark the beginning and end of a quiet zone.  
 
Rail Train  
Rail Trains consist of flat cars coupled together with or without special mountings for handling lengths of rail extending from car 
to car for transport.    
 
Railroad-supplied electronic or electrical device  
An electronic or electrical device provided to a railroad operating employee by the employing railroad for one or more business 
purposes.  
 
Soft Cut Out (PTC):  
A state of the PTC system resulting from selection of the cut-out key on the PTC display.  
 
Switch Control Signs  
Signs placed approximately 2 miles from a Power Assisted Switch. These signs mark areas where crew members must begin 
switch alignment or switch verification procedures.  
 
Tabular General Bulletin Order (TGBO) – a document providing, in a tabular format, the information or instructions contained 
in each track bulletin, which affect a train or engine within specified limits.

Spur tracks and Terminals that have changes will be listed on the subdivision they are connected to as identified in Timetable 
subdivision footnotes.   
 
1.3.4 Facsimile Machines 
Crew member, upon reporting for work at locations not equipped with a Field Information Terminal (FIT) and only equipped with 
FAX machines will request the documents needed and after receiving same, crew must ascertain that the documents are legible 
and complete. 
 
In the event the FAX machine fails to function as intended or documents are not complete, crew member must communicate with 
the train dispatcher and be governed by instructions received. 
 
1.5 Drugs and Alcohol - is changed to read:  
The use or possession of alcoholic beverages, while on duty, on company property or while occupying facilities paid for or 
furnished by the company (including any required or instructed medical procedures and examinations) is prohibited. Employees 
must not have any measurable alcohol in their breath or in their bodily fluids when reporting for duty, while on duty, while on 
company property, or while occupying facilities paid for or furnished by the company (including any required or instructed medical 
procedures and examinations).  
 
The use or possession of intoxicants, over the counter or prescription drugs, narcotics, controlled substances, or medication that 
may adversely affect safe performance is prohibited while on duty, while on company property, or while occupying facilities paid 
for or furnished by the company (including any required or instructed medical procedures and examinations). Employees must 
not possess, sell, use, or have in their bodily fluids any illegal drug or controlled substance while on or off duty except medication 
that is permitted by a medical practitioner and used as prescribed. 
 
1.6 Conduct – is changed by adding the following paragraph as the last paragraph:  
Desertion from duty, making false reports or statements and concealing facts concerning matters under investigation are 
prohibited.  Any violation of the law that is determined by the Carrier to make an employee unsuitable for railroad employment is 
grounds for dismissal. 
 
1.11 Sleeping – is changed to read: 
Employees must not sleep while on duty. Employees slouched or reclined with their eyes closed or concealed will be in 
violation of this rule. 
 
1.11.1 Napping - Rule does not apply on CPKC.

Section 3 – General Code of Operating Rules – Special Instructions 
 
22 
 
 
1.17 (B) Hours of Service Law – is added as last sentence as follows: 
In the event service is rendered in excess of the Hours-of-Service law for any reason, conductor, foreman or other employees 
must submit a complete report, providing all details, to the appropriate supervisor’s office within 24 hours or the next tour of duty. 
 
1.28 Fire is changed to read: 
Employees must report promptly to the train dispatcher any fires seen on or near the right of way unless the fires are being 
controlled. If there is danger of the fire spreading to a bridge or other structure, “trained” crew members must stop their train and 
help extinguish the fire. Cause of fire, if known, must be promptly reported. 
 
1.30 Riding Engines - following added as the last paragraph:  
Exception - Trains operating in yards, must have one employee (when there are two or more employees on the locomotive) 
positioned on the footboard or platform of the leading locomotive in the direction of travel within 500 feet of a switch until the 
movement fully occupies the switch to observe proper alignment. This rule also applies while operating on foreign carriers. 
 
1.34 Flat Spots – is added to as follows:  
When equipment is set out due to flat spots, train dispatcher must be notified, and equipment must also be shown on train delay 
report. Locomotives must not be set out without authority from the train dispatcher. 
 
1.36 Excessive Dimension Loads - Overload Policy: 
The following outlines the acceptance and furtherance of shipments loaded in four axle freight cars equipped with roller bearings

2.21 Electronic Devices – is changed to read as follows: 
2.21 Electronic Devices 
This rule outlines the requirements for the use of electronic devices. Crew members are jointly responsible for compliance with 
the appropriate use of electronic devices. 
 
Electronic Device - An electronic or electrical device used to conduct oral, written, or visual communication; place or receive a 
telephone call; send or read an electronic mail message or text message; look at pictures; read a book or other written material; 
play a game; navigate the Internet; navigate the physical world; play, view, or listen to a video; play, view or listen to a television 
broadcast; play or listen to music; execute a computational function; or, perform any other function that is not necessary for the 
health or safety of the person and that entails the risk of distracting the employee or another employee from a safety related task. 
 
The use of any electronic device is prohibited if that use would interfere with an employee’s performance of safety-related duties. 
 
Railroad Supplied Electronic Devices 
Railroad operating employees may use railroad supplied electronic devices to send or receive work related for authorized 
business purposes. Care and good judgement must always be used to ensure proper attention and concentration when 
performing any task. 
 
Railroad operating employees must not use a railroad supplied electronic device for purposes other than which it was intended 
or while: 
• 
Inside or outside the controlling cab of a locomotive, train or on-track equipment, unless there has been a safety briefing, 
and all crew members agree that it is safe to do so. 
• 
Operating the controls of a moving locomotive unless device is being used to reference a railroad rule, special instruction, 
timetable, track elevation chart or other directive and use does not interfere with any employee’s performance of safety 
related duties. 
• 
On the ground within 4 feet of any track. 
• 
On the ground and engaged in an active switching operation. 
• 
Riding rolling equipment during a switching operation. 
• 
At the controls of the locomotive and any other employee is assisting in the preparation of the train, engine(s), or on-track 
equipment, including testing of railroad equipment or brakes. 
 
Railroad authorized electronic devices may be used in the body of a business car or passenger train for railroad business when 
it will not interfere with an employee’s performance of safety related duties.  
 
Personal Electronic Devices  
A. Prohibited Use: 
All personal electronic devices are prohibited and must be turned off, stored out of sight and not on your person with any earpieces 
removed from the ear.

6.0 Movement of Trains and Engines 
6.1.1 Verbal Communication – New Rule added as follows: 
Crew members are jointly responsible to make verbal communication between each other and confirm it is properly understood 
when any of the following work activities apply to them: 
• Required brake tests are completed, 
• switches are properly lined and/or locked, visually confirming route to be used, 
• derails are properly applied or removed and visually checked, 
• handbrakes are applied or released, 
• shove movements are protected, 
• employees are getting on or off moving equipment, 
• employees crossing between equipment, 
• when a situation changes, 
• when entering a track with restricted clearance, 
• when cars are left out to foul another track during switching, 
• before entering a classification track in a hump yard, 
• before entering a main track to confirm movement authority,  
• before reporting a track release, 
  or 
• when equipment is left unattended, confirming securement effectiveness. 
 
This rule will also apply to other employees, where applicable. 
 
6.2 Initiating Movement – the following added as last paragraph: 
When an Out of Service tag is applied to the locomotive’s throttle, control stand or location readily visible to the engineer, the 
engine must not be moved until contact is made with the employee in charge whose name is on the Out of Service tag to establish 
working limits and permission to move equipment.

Section 3 – General Code of Operating Rules – Special Instructions 
 
28 
 
6.2.1 Train Location – is changed to read as follows: 
Trains or maintenance of way employees who receive authority to occupy the main track after the arrival of a train or to follow a 
train must ascertain the train’s location by one of the following methods:  
• 
Direct communication with a crew member of the train 
or  
• 
Receiving information about the train from the train dispatcher or control operator. 
 
Train crews providing a train location must use a specific location that the entire train is complete by. 
Note: Maintenance of Way employees issued authority to occupy a main track or controlled siding behind or do not foul limits 
ahead of a train, must advise the train that working limits have been established behind their train. Trains so informed must not 
make a reverse movement except as prescribed per GCOR 6.4.1 (Permission for Reverse Movements) 
 
6.3 Main Track Authorization – under Joint Authority the following is added after the last bullet  
(US Eastern Region and the Kansas City Subdivision ONLY): 
Employees contacted for permission to enter joint authority limits will designate name of employee in charge and state location 
of their working limits. Employee in charge and employee receiving will record this information on the working limits form. Once 
this information is received, repeated, and recorded, movements may then move into the joint limits. Once clear of the working 
limits the movement must inform the employee in charge of the working limits. 
 
If more than one employee is listed within the joint authority, one employee may be assigned as the employee in charge for all 
other employees listed within the joint limits. The employee in charge will state this in instructions given to other movements, 
giving names of other employees under their working limits. Contact with other employee(s) in this case is not necessary. 
 
Instructions and information may be relayed through the train dispatcher or other employees for the employee in charge. 
 
Trains must move at restricted speed within joint authorities. When trains are given joint authorities with other trains, contact with 
each train is not required.  
 
6.5 Shove Movements – First paragraph is changed to read as follows: 
Equipment must not be shoved until the engineer and the employee protecting the movement have completed a job briefing 
concerning how protection will be provided. Once the employee who will be protecting the shove movement is in position, verbal 
verification will be made between the Engineer and the person protecting the shove movement that will include all switches, 
derails, gates, or obstructions pertaining to shove move have either been lined properly or removed.  The employee protecting 
the shove movement must be in position to provide visual protection of the intended route of equipment being shoved, must not 
be inside of any vehicle and should not be engaged in unrelated tasks while providing protection.

4. When relieved from providing protection, the remote-control operator must remain outside of any vehicle or building until the 
movement is complete.

A switch equipped with a switch point lock pedal will be identified by a white or yellow stripe on both sides of the switch stand or

locks are secured on both the switch and switch point lock after use. 
 
8.12 Crossover Switches - is added to as follows: 
When switch tenders are on duty for handling main track switches for crossover movements, the following procedure must be 
followed: 
1. 
Switch tenders on duty must have a copy of the track bulletin or a message in the exact words of the track bulletin prior 
to commencing the day’s work. 
2.

3.

8.16 Damaged or Defective Switches - is added to as follows: 
When switches are spiked, they will be identified by a tag or tape attached to the switch stand or handle. This does not relieve 
the requirements of additional protection as required. 
 
8.18 Variable Switches - rule does not apply on CPKC property.  
Crews are to hand line all trailing movements through switches regardless of if it is a variable switch or not. Designated spring 
switches are the only switches that would be able to be trailed through when not lined for the movement. 
 
8.19.1 Radio Controlled Switches (RCS) or Power Assisted Switches (PAS) 
The location of Radio-Controlled Switches or Power Assisted Switches and operating instructions will be designated in the 
timetable and/or special instructions.  
 
A Radio-Controlled Switch or Power Assisted Switch can be remotely controlled by using the radio keypad on the channel so 
indicated under the subdivision footnotes, or by using a push button located at the switch in a box mounted on the signal case.  
 
At Radio Controlled Switch or Power Assisted Switch locations there will be "Begin OS" and "End OS" signs marking the limits 
of the on switch. In order for the RCS or PAS to operate by DTMF or by push button located at the switch; the limits of the OS 
must not be occupied.   
 
8.19.2 Operating a Radio-Controlled Switch (RCS) or Power Assisted Switch (PAS)  
To operate a Radio-Controlled Switch (RCS) or Power Assisted Switch (PAS), a crew member must perform the following:   
Upon passing the wayside sign reading "switch control" (Placed approximately 2 miles from an RCS or PAS), a crew member 
must enter the proper DTMF sequence for the desired switch position.   
 
NOTE: Switch Control signs installed less than two miles from an RCS or PAS location will be noted in the Timetable.   
 
To enter the proper DTMF sequence:   
To line the switch to the normal or reverse position, enter the code found in the Timetable. After entering the proper DTMF 
sequence, you must receive radio confirmation that the switch is properly lined for requested movement.   
 
A train must approach an RSC or PAS prepared to stop short of the OS until:   
1. 
A DTMF command has been issued to request the switch for the desired position and radio confirmation message has 
been received that the switch is properly lined for desired movement. Crew on movement must repeat radio messages 
received from a radio-controlled switch.  
or   
2. 
The switch point indicator displays the switch is properly lined, as per GCOR 8.10, for the requested movement.   
 
The switch point indicator will convey the following indication to the movement:  
Green – radio activated switch is lined and locked for main track movement.  
Flashing Red or Yellow – radio activated switch is lined and locked for diverging movement.  
Red – Stop, inspect switch, and then operate dual control switch by hand in accordance with GCOR 9.13.1.  Permission to 
hand operate is not necessary if movement authority is granted beyond switch or movement is to take siding.  
Dark – Stop, inspect switch, and then operate dual control switch by hand in accordance with GCOR 9.13.1.  Permission to 
hand operate is not necessary if movement authority is granted beyond switch or movement is to take siding.  
 
If a movement receives a dark or red indicator it must be reported to the train dispatcher/operation supervisor.  
 
Dark indicator will indicate one or combinations of the following conditions.   
• That the RCS or PAS is unable to verify request  
• The RCS or PAS switch is not locked in position

36 
 
NOTE: If the train has not passed the Switch Point Indicator within 10 minutes after a confirmation message is received that the 
switch is properly lined for movement, the train must approach the RCS or PAS prepared to stop.

9.0 Block System Rules 
9.5.3 Protection during Repairs 
Track bulletin Form B will not be used for protection within manual interlocking limits. Rest of rule remains unchanged. 
 
9.8 Next Governing Signal – is changed to read:  
A train may comply with the next signal’s indication when its aspect can be clearly seen, and the signal governs the track where 
movement is occurring or will be made. When operating in PTC Full Enforcement Mode and the PTC Display indicates the next 
governing signal will allow the train to proceed, or increase speed, the train may proceed complying with the signal indication 
governing the next block. This does not apply when a rule or previous signal indication requires movement at restricted speed.  
 
9.9 Train Delayed Within a Block – Item B CTC or Manual Interlocking Limits – is changed to read:  
Proceed prepared to stop at the next signal until the next signal is visible and that signal displays a proceed indication. When 
operating in PTC Full Enforcement Mode and the PTC Display indicates the next governing signal will allow the train to proceed, 
or increase speed, the train may proceed complying with the signal indication governing the next block. Passenger trains 
operating in push/pull service must not exceed 40 MPH until the next signal is visible and that signal displays a proceed indication. 
 
9.9.1 Approach to Automatic Interlocking  
A train must proceed prepared to stop at the interlocking signal when:  
• 
Moving below 25 MPH and passing a signal that governs the approach to an automatic  interlocking.  
or  
• 
Speed is reduced below 25 MPH after passing a signal that governs the approach to an automatic interlocking.  
 
When the Automatic Interlocking contains an Interlocking Approach (IA) circuit, IA milepost locations will be listed in the Timetable 
Subdivision Special Instructions and may be identified in the field by "Begin Interlocking Approach" signs. The train must proceed 
prepared to stop at the interlocking signal when: 
 
• 
Speed is at or reduced below 25 MPH after passing a milepost location designated as the beginning of the Interlocking 
Approach (IA) circuit.  
 
The train must continue to move prepared to stop at the interlocking signal until the train reaches a point approximately 1,000 
feet from that signal. If the interlocking signal, then indicates proceed, the train may resume speed.  
 
9.12.1 (CTC Territory) and 9.12.2 (Manual Interlocking) the following is added as last sentence to third bullet:  
Before proceeding from a Stop indication, crew member must examine each dual control switch to see that it is properly lined for 
the route to be used and must remain on ground until movement occupies the route.  This does not apply to passenger trains 
that have a single engineer in the control cab.  
 
9.12.3 Automatic Interlockings - is changed to read:  
At a signal displaying a Stop indication, the crew will be governed by instructions in the release box, special instructions, or other 
instructions. If required to operate release box, train must pull to within 200’ of signal before operating. After complying with the 
instructions that allow the train to proceed, if signal continues to display a Stop indication, the train must move at restricted speed 
after receiving a signal from the employee on the ground at the crossing. However, if there is a conflicting movement, the train 
must not proceed until the movement has passed or stopped, and both crews agree on the next movement. 
 
At an automatic interlocking where push buttons are provided on signals to enable a return movement to be made over the 
crossing while switching, crew member will unlock box and press button. If signal does not clear, requirements of GCOR 9.12.3 
must be complied with. 
 
9.15.2 Clearing Track Permits – the following is added below the bullet points. 
Before an employee reports clear of a track permit, the report must be confirmed with another employee, if more than one 
employee is present.  
 
After a release is given to the train dispatcher/control operator with the required information, the train dispatcher/control operator 
will repeat it back to the employee for confirmation.  
 
Employee or in the case of a train the Engineer will confirm the repeat back from the control operator and will also state their 
occupation and name. 
 
Track permit will remain in effect until the train dispatcher/control operator confirms the release back.

15.0 Track Bulletin Rules 
In Chapter 15 - Track Bulletin Rules, wherever the changes refer to Tabular General Bulletin Order (TGBO) it will also   
imply to Track Bulletin (TB). 
Rule 15.1 – Track Bulletins – under Receipt and Comparison of Track Bulletins is changed to read as follows: 
RECEIPT AND COMPARISON  
At their initial station, unless otherwise instructed by the train dispatcher or special instructions, the conductor and engineer must 
each receive and have a copy of the Tabular General Bulletin Order (TGBO) affecting their train’s movement on a main track. 
Any pilot or snowplow foreman must each be in possession of the TGBO for their movement. 
 
The conductor and engineer must confirm and initial the train designation, the TGBO designated limits, and each page of the 
TGBO and then sign the last page of their TGBO.  Other crew member(s) will be required to read and understand the TGBO 
then initial and sign the TGBO they reviewed. 
 
All crew members must ensure that their movement is properly designated on the TGBO, it contains the correct number of pages 
and that the designated limits cover the specified routing.   
 
If it will not cause delay to movement, freight trains and road switchers should contact train dispatcher to confirm and verify 
TGBO number. 
 
A train specific TGBO will be addressed to a train symbol, assignment number or schedule number, and must be compared to a 
train consist, list or other acceptable document for verification.  If an incorrectly designated TGBO is received train dispatcher 
must be contacted for further instructions or changes before proceeding. Engine identifying number is not required on a TGBO. 
If a movement receives a TGBO that shows NIL for Track Bulletins, contact the Train Dispatcher to verify the information before 
acting on the TGBO.    
 
At locations where yard limits are in effect and a train or engine cannot get their train specific TGBO, they may use a generic 
default TGBO to perform work within yard limits.  Crew must obtain their train specific TGBO before going outside of yard limits.   
Passenger trains that do not have a schedule number will be addressed using engine number adding direction as applicable.  
 
When a crew member receives a TGBO from the Field Informational Terminal (FIT), once verified that the document is correct, 
the crew member will acknowledge the prompt on the screen of the FIT before leaving. If the TGBO is pulled from the FIT by 
anyone other than a crew member, such as a Clerk, they will acknowledge the prompt on the screen by entering their Occupation, 
Initials and Last Name and check the box as the Acknowledger. The crew is still responsible to verify that the information 
contained in the document is correct. If unable to obtain a TGBO from the FIT or FAX contact the train dispatcher for further 
instructions.  
 
TGBO’s will have lines in ascending order. Lines must be checked for ascending sequence, if they are not, then that TGBO is 
not complete, crew member must communicate with the train dispatcher and be governed by instructions received. 
 
All crew members are responsible for complying with the requirements of track bulletins in the TGBO and for reminding each 
other of those requirements. 
 
15.1.1 Changing Address of Track Warrant or Track Bulletins – is changed to read: 
15.1.1 Changing Address of Tabular General Bulletin Order  
If the designation on the TGBO is incorrect, a change of designation must be issued by the train dispatcher.  If the designation 
of the train consist list or other acceptable document is incorrect and the TGBO designation is correct, the designation may be 
changed when authorized by the train dispatcher, company officer or other employee who has access to the correct information. 
Metra scheduled trains using train specific TGBO’s may change train designation in address with verbal authority from the train 
dispatcher.

Section 4 – Radios 
 
Transmitting Technique 
The efficient use of a radio depends on the speech and articulation of the sender.  Speak all words plainly in a clear, distinct 
tone to prevent the running together of consecutive words.  DO NOT SHOUT.  Avoid any tendency to accent syllables artificially 
or talk too rapidly.  Speak slowly and clearly. 
 
The following points should be kept in mind when using a radio: 
Position of Microphone:  Microphone should be angled at approximately 45 degrees, not more than 2 to 3 inches from the 
mouth of the sender. 
Speed:  Keep the rate constant, neither too fast nor too slow.  Remember in many cases the person receiving your message 
has to write it down. 
Pitch:  Remember, that high pitched voices transmit better than low pitched ones. 
Rhythm:  Preserve the rhythm of ordinary conversation.  To separate words so that they do not run together, avoid the 
introduction of sound that does not belong such as “er” and “um.”   Attempt to maintain the pitch and rhythm of voice to the end 
of each sentence.

Section 5 – Trackside Warning Detectors 
 
1.0 Trackside Warning Detector  
1.1 General 
Trackside Warning Detectors operate for trains in either direction on the track in which they are installed. Each detector type and 
location are listed in each subdivision footnotes along with recall codes, where provided, and will indicate one or more of the following: 
 
Detector Type 
Description  
Hot Box (HBD) 
Detects overheated journals. Hot Box alarms can also be caused by overheated 
traction motor suspension bearings and sticking brakes. 
Dragging Equipment (DED) 
Detects equipment dragging between or near the rails. 
High Wide Load Detector (HWLD) 
Detects shipments exceeding acceptable height and width dimensions.  
High Water Detector 
Measures water level near track and indicates using a signaling system of 
condition requiring train crew stop. 
Wheel Impact Load Detector (WILD) 
Measures excessive wheel impact on rail and identify defective cars using AEI 
car tag IDs. 
Additional information from Detector 
Description  
Axle Count 
Counts axles in train and reports it after entire train passes the detector. May 
include axle location as part of a defect message. 
Temperature 
Measures outside temperature and reports it after the entire train passes the 
Trackside Warning Detector. Temperature may be used in the application of Hot 
and Cold Weather Temperature Speed Restrictions. 
 
1.2 Alarm Announcements and Procedures while Approaching/Passing Trackside Warning Detectors 
As the train passes the detector, the talker transmits an alert tone and announcement for each alarm. The following table summarizes 
the announcements and procedures when approaching and passing a Trackside Warning Detector. 
 
Alarm Announcements while passing a Trackside Warning Detectors 
Alarm Type 
Announcement   
Hot Box  
Tone + “hot box” or Tone + “hot journal” 
Dragging Equipment  
Tone + “dragging equipment” 
Hot Wheel 
Tone + “hot wheel”  
High Wide Load 
Tone + “high load” or Tone + “wide load” or Tone + “high car” 
High Water  
No tone 
When approaching a Trackside Warning Detector 
Locomotive Engineer  
Must avoid prolonged use of train brakes where practicable, until the entire train passes the 
detector.  
All Crew Members 
Must ensure the train radio is on the correct standby channel.

sections.text:
1.3 After Passing a Trackside Warning Detector – Final Results 
Use this table to identify the appropriate Trackside Warning Detector procedure for various events. 
 
 
Event  
Procedure  
A 
Final results message reports “No Defects” or 
“Proceed”  
Proceed without an inspection. 
B 
No final results message received  
a) The crew must attempt to initiate a rebroadcast of the 
detector message using the recall code listed in the 
Timetable.  
b) If any announcement and/or alert tones were heard, then 
inspect the entire train following the procedures in items 
1.4 Dragging Equipment, 1.5 Hot Box, 1.6 Hot Wheel or 
1.7 High Wide Load as applicable.  
c) If you are a Key or Alert Train and no announcement 
and/or alert tones are heard, then proceed per second 
paragraph in 1.11 No Defect Found – Key Train, Alert 
Train, or Key/Alert Train. 
C 
Final results message reports “system not working”, 
“system test failure”, “system failure” or “integrity 
failure”  
D 
Defect announced while passing the HBD, but  
message unclear or in doubt 
Reduce to Slow Speed and listen carefully to the final 
message if not yet received. The crew must attempt to initiate 
a rebroadcast of the detector message using the recall code 
listed in the Timetable. If unable to do so, notify dispatcher 
and inspect the entire train following the procedures in items 
1.4 Dragging Equipment, 1.5 Hot Box, 1.6 Hot Wheel or 1.7 
High Wide Load as applicable. 
E 
Final results message reports defect, but the  
location is not heard or is in doubt 
F 
Speed is 8 MPH or less passing an operating HBD and 
final results message reports NO defect 
If you are a Key or Alert Train and no announcement and/or 
alert tones are heard, then proceed per second paragraph in 
1.11 No Defect Found – Key Train, Alert Train, or Key/Alert 
Train. 
G 
HBD withdrawn from service by GBO/DOB or by 
Operating Bulletin 
H 
Speed is 8 MPH or less passing an operating HBD and 
final results message reports a defect 
Inspect the entire train following the procedures in items 1.4 
Dragging Equipment, 1.5 Hot Box, 1.6 Hot Wheel or 1.7 High 
Wide Load as applicable. 
I 
Defect: Hot box or Hot Journal announced while 
passing HBD 
See item 1.5 Hot Box 
J 
Defect: Hot wheel announced while passing  
HBD 
See item 1.6 Hot Wheel 
K 
Defect: Dragging equipment announced  
while passing dragger/HBD  
See item 1.4 Dragging Equipment 
L 
Defect: High load, wide load or high car announced 
while passing a high wide load detector.  
See item 1.7 High Wide Load when a high wide load detector 
is temporarily removed from service or, if final results 
message not received or reports system not working, entire 
train must be inspected for height restrictions before passing 
under height restricted areas. 
M 
Incorrect axle count and the final results message 
reports No defects 
See item 1.13 Incorrect Axle Count. 
N 
Any announcement from a trackside warning detector 
Verbal communication between crew members of message 
content is required for any wayside detector message. Radio 
acknowledgment of results will be transmitted using proper 
radio procedure. 
 
Note (False Alarm): Train crews may be informed by the Dispatcher that an inspection is not required due to a false alarm as

sections.text:
1.4 Dragging Equipment  
 
 
1.5 Hot Box 
 
When an alert tone is followed by the announcement “hot box” …  
Step 
Action  
1 
Note the DMD reading. 
2 
Immediately reduce to Slow Speed using throttle modulation and dynamic brake, and without using the air brakes, if 
possible.  
• 
If a subsequent announcement states “dragging equipment” or the train will pass over a facing point switch, 
then stop immediately and follow the procedure for dragging equipment. 
3 
Observe the train for defects. If the defect is visible from the cab of the locomotive or there is an  
obvious indication of a derailment, then stop the train immediately and inspect. (See item 1.9 Procedures for Locating 
Defects) 
4 
When the rear of the train has passed the HBD, and the final results messages have been reported.  
• 
allow a crew member to detrain, and  
• 
pull the train ahead, not exceeding 10 MPH, to the defect.  
Note: If an inspection point is designated, then proceed, not exceeding 10 MPH (without stopping) to the inspection 
point.   
Note 
If the final results message reports more than six alarms, stop the train immediately and perform a stationary inspection 
(dragging equipment procedure applies).  
Exception: an uninspected portion of the train will not pass over a facing point switch, a pull-by inspection or 
combination standing/pull-by inspection is permitted at a speed not exceeding 5 MPH.  During the  
pull-by portion, the back of the hand inspection should be used to test for overheated bearing(s).  A stationary inspection 
must also be performed for any suspect defects found and at the location where the “hot box” announcement(s) was 
broadcast, based on DMD calculations.  
Note 
If the final results message reports “No Alarms” then resume speed and proceed without an inspection. 
5 
Perform a stationary inspection at the defect location.  
a) Locate the defect using the axle count as per item 1.9 Procedures for Locating Defects.  
b) See item 2.1 Hot Box Inspection–Friction and Roller Bearing, to test for overheated bearings. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
When an alert tone is followed by the announcement “dragging equipment” … 
Step 
Action  
1 
Note the DMD reading. 
2 
Stop the train immediately using good train handling practices. 
3 
Perform a stationary train inspection.  
a) 
If the entire train passes the HBD location before stopping, then locate the defect using the  
axle count as per item 1.9  Procedures for Locating Defects). 
b) 
If the train is stopped before the entire movement passes the HBD, then locate the defect using the noted 
DMD distance as per item 1.9  Procedures for Locating Defects). 
Note 
Do not pull ahead to a crew member to perform the inspection unless it is unsafe to walk back. If it is unsafe to walk 
back, then pull ahead not exceeding 5 MPH to inspect for defect.  
If the train must be pulled ahead over a facing point switch, do not exceed 5 MPH.

sections.title: 1.9 Procedures for Locating Defects
sections.text:
1.9 Procedures for Locating Defects 
 
Step 
Action  
1 
• 
Note the axle location of the defects stated in the final results message, or  
• 
Determine the approximate location of the defect by using the noted DMD distance and train consist 
information  
2 
If determining defect location by axle count, locate the defects by counting the actual axles from the front of the train, 
beginning with the lead locomotive. Ensure cars and locomotives with other than four axles are not counted as having 
four axles. 
3 
• 
If defect is other than dragging equipment, a pull-by inspection to the point of the identified defect, may be 
made provided if there is no obvious indication of derailment and speed of inspection does not exceed 10 
MPH. 
• 
If a defect indication is for dragging equipment, a walking inspection must be made while the train is stationary. 
While performing the walking inspection and conditions no longer permit safe walking, the train may be pulled 
ahead not exceeding 5 MPH to the identified axle. 
4 
Inspect the train in the specified location.  
• 
If a defect is found at or near the indicated location, then inspect both sides of the train for 8 axles in each 
direction from the suspected defect. (This helps verify that the defect has been correctly identified.)  
• 
If a defect is not found at the indicated location, then inspect both sides of the train for 16 axles in each 
direction from the indicated location. 
• 
If a defect is detected at a High or Wide Load Detector, in addition to checking the location specified, two cars 
(or two platforms) ahead and behind the reported location must also be inspected, even if defect is found at 
the reported location. 
5 
If any part of the train passed the HBD at 8 MPH or less, then inspect the entire train for additional defects. 
6 
Notify the Dispatcher of the inspection results and take appropriate action  
(e.g., make repairs, set off car, etc.). 
7 
Complete the required reporting documentation.  
8 
If the defect was a suspected hot box and no defect was found, see item 1.10, No Defect Found. 
Note - Alarms from hot wheel detectors and dragging equipment detectors can only indicate the general vicinity of the alarm, 
rather than an exact location. During inspection process, be governed by Section 2 Train Inspection Procedures 
 
1.10 No Defect Found  
If no defects are found after the inspection process, train may proceed at maximum authorized speed, watching train accordingly, 
except Key Trains will be governed by 1.11 No Defect Found – Key/Alert Train. 
 
When a Hot Journal/Hot Wheel alarm is received and no defect is found the inbound crew must notify the connecting crew of any 
defects providing the defective equipment initial and number, axle count(s), side of car(s) and defect(s). If the last system encountered 
failed, the inbound crew must notify the connecting crew of such failure. If connecting crew is not available this information must be 
properly documented and left on the console of the lead locomotive. When a Hot Journal alarm is received on an axle that has been 
previously marked with a “W” the car must be set out.  
 
Second Defect within 75 miles 
Whenever a car or engine is identified by an alarm for the defect “hot box” at the same axle location twice within 75 miles car or engine 
must be set out of train. 
 
Exception:  Business car CP 99 (Display car) is equipped with a low-slung generator that when operating may trigger a false “Hot 
Box” alarm. Providing business car personnel perform a bearing temperature test and no excessive temperature is present, CP 99 is 
exempt from the requirement of setting it out of train.  
 
Second Defect in Succession 
When the same car or engine is identified by an alarm for a defect at a second trackside warning detector in succession, the car or 
engine must be set out of the train regardless of whether or not a defect can be found. While moving car to be set out, you must 
maintain a speed that will ensure safe handling of the car, but not exceeding ten (10) MPH.

1.11 No Defect Found – Key Train, Alert Train, or Key/Alert Train 
If no defects are found, a Key Train, Alert Train or Key/Alert Train will not exceed 30 MPH until it has passed over the next working 
trackside-warning detector or is delivered to a terminal for a mechanical inspection. If the same car sets off the next trackside-warning 
detector or is found to be defective, it must be set out from the train.  
 
When a Key Train, Alert Train or Key/Alert Train is informed that a trackside-warning detector is out of service the Key/Alert Train will 
be restricted to 30 MPH from the out of service trackside-warning detector to the next working track side warning detector. 
 
1.12 Trackside Warning Detector - Alarm Reporting Exceeded 
When a trackside warning detector exceeds 6 defects, the trackside warning detector will report too many alarms and then report a 
malfunction. 
 
When this type of alarm is sounded, train must be promptly stopped, and a stationary train inspection must be made at the reported 
axle locations and the rest of the entire train on both sides to the rear of the last reported axle location must be inspected. 
 
Notation must be made on Crew Information Form and train list of cars showing the location of detector(s) that indicated car defect.

When a trackside warning detector indicates a one axle plus or minus difference in comparison with the number of axles known to be 
in the train, proceed at maximum authorized speed.

governed as follows: 
 
Step 
Action  
1 
Advise train dispatcher of incorrect axle count and arrange to verify the trains consist information. Train may continue 
to move at maximum authorized speed. Key Trains will proceed not exceeding 30 MPH to next detector. 
2 
If the train is carrying an additional car or cars and any of these are hazardous, arrange for a radio waybill. Update 
the position-in-train document for hazardous materials. 
3 
Continue to the next trackside warning detector and verify axle count with that detector.  If the axle count still does not 
match, stop, and perform a pull by inspection.  During inspection, pay close attention to wheel condition and low-
hanging equipment next to wheels, i.e., cables, banding, chains, or plastic wrapping.

If no defects are found after inspection, the train may proceed at maximum authorized speed.  Notify the train

Communicate the correct information to the next outbound crew or proper supervisor.

sections.title: 2.0 Train Inspection Procedures
sections.text:
2.0 Train Inspection Procedures 
When informed by a trackside warning detector or other source of a possible hot wheel, hot bearing or dragging equipment, an 
inspection must be made.  This alarm may result from abnormal heat from wheels (sticking brakes), journals, traction motors, or 
suspension bearings. At trackside warning detector locations, also comply with trackside warning detector instructions. 
 
2.1 Hot Box Inspection–Friction and Roller Bearing 
 
A 
 Required Equipment:  
All crew members, other than locomotive engineers, of each movement must be in  possession of a temperature 
indicating  crayon (150ºF). 
B 
 Crayon Application:  
 Use crayon as per illustrations in Diagrams 1, 3 and 4 below.  
 Crayon may not melt at or below freezing. 
C 
 Inspection Procedure: 
• Inspection for suspected overheating must include the use of the temperature indicating crayon or if no crayon is 
available, feeling the roller bearing housing using the back of the bare hand. CAUTION: When using the back of the 
hand, do not physically touch the bearing housing if excessive heat is felt as your hand approaches the bearing 
housing or axle. 
• When using the temperature crayon, the employee performing the duties must mark the bearing housing and end 
bolt(s) with sufficient force with the crayon to make an identifiable mark to indicate that it has been checked. (see 
Diagram 1).  
• In all cases, inspection must be as instructed by Section 5, item 1.9 Procedures for Locating Defects, Item 4 which 
requires an inspection of  8 axles in both directions, both sides from a defect that is found and 16 axles in both 
direction, both sides if no defect is found.  
D 
 Crayon Results:  
 Wax-like, shiny smear indicates overheated bearing as illustrated in Diagram 2 below.  
Thin, colored line indicates the metal is  not overheated (i.e., metal is below the  temperature indicated on the crayon). 
E 
 Overheated Bearing Confirmed: 
• Set out the car at the first available location or location designated in the Timetable. 
• Complete Crew Information Form and report to the Dispatcher. 
 
Use a marker to write the date and the letter “X” above each journal found to be overheated and set out. Write the date and the 
letter “W” above each wheel indicated if no defect is found and the car remains in the train.

2.2 Hot Wheel 
When inspecting for an overheated or hot wheel, pre-departure or while en route the wheels should be checked for heat discoloration 
of any type. If discoloration or bluing of the wheel extends more than 4 inches from the rim to the plate, on both the front face and

b) Safety Defect:

sections.title: 2.3 Dragging Equipment
sections.text:
2.3 Dragging Equipment 
In case of dragging equipment indication, STOP the train immediately using good train handling procedures and perform a walking 
inspection to the indicated location. Look for equipment or material that extends below the ball of the rail. Common items to look for 
are hanging brake shoes, brake shoe keys, brake riggings, low hanging air hoses, tie-down bands, wire, or chains. When defect is 
found and repaired or it is safe to move the equipment, a roll-by inspection of the remainder of the train must be made with speed 
not exceeding 10 MPH.   
 
Clear dragging equipment if possible for safe running, and if not safe to run, the car should be set out at the nearest point. 
 
2.4 Other Wheel Defect Inspections 
When inspecting wheels for a wheel defect, look for broken flange, thin flange, broken rim, loose wheel, flat spots, wheels with metal 
build up, extra-long brake shoe keys, brake rigging hanging down or dragging.  
 
To determine if a wheel is loose, examine it for the following: 
1. Excessive spacing between the wheel flange and the rail. 
2. Heavy cuttings on the wheel flange. 
3. Particles of metal on the inside of the wheel seat or axle. 
4. A shiny area on the axle near the wheel. 
5. Oil seepage around the wheel seat and axle. 
 
If no defect is found, perform an audible inspection by listening for sounds of a broken wheel, flat spots, or any other defect that 
may be present. Audible inspection will be performed by positioning yourself 10 cars ahead of the reported defect and roll the train 
by 20 cars listening for indications of a defect. If no axle number is given, an audible inspection of the entire train must be completed. 
 
Set the car out if a sound is heard suggesting a broken wheel (thumping sound) or any other sound or visual indication that may 
indicate a defect. 
 
2.5 Warm Wheel Notification Process 
The Warm Wheel Notification Process is like the WILD Detector procedure, in that the hot box detectors will be used to monitor for 
sticking brakes or hand brakes based on increased wheel temperature levels.  These levels are lower than those that would normally 
trigger a hot wheel alarm. 
 
If a sticking airbrake/handbrake is identified, an alert message will be generated to the Dispatcher that will advise of the alarm type 
and what recommended actions to be communicated to the train crew. This is separate from a sticking brake alarm that is broadcast 
from the detector itself. 
 
Crews are also reminded of the requirement to ensure that an effective 10 psi reduction is made to ensure that it propagates 
throughout the train before the release is made.  
 
The following indicates the process when a warm wheel notification is received from the Dispatcher.

sections.text:
3.2 Setting out Defective Cars 
A defective car must be set out whenever it cannot be safely moved to the next repair location. Before cars are set out, a report of 
this fact must be made to the train dispatcher. When setting out defective cars the following will apply: 
1. Set out mechanically defective cars where Mechanical Service employees can access them. On some tracks a sign will 
indicate “Set Bad Order Wheel Here” or by yellow markings on rail, in this case the bad order will be set out with the bad 
wheel at the sign or at yellow markings. 
2. If the bearing is overheated, inspect the underside of the car.  
3. Put out any fires before leaving the car. 
4. When a derailed car with roller bearings is re-railed by other than Mechanical Service Employees, move it carefully to a set 
out point for inspection and maintenance. 
5. Do not exceed 5 MPH while handling the defective car and watch it closely so that a prompt stop can be made if the car 
derails. 
 
3.3 Train Dispatcher Notification 
After any defect inspection notify the train dispatcher with the following information as it applies: 
• Location of trackside warning detector, if applicable. 
• Car initial and number. 
• Wheel number and side 
• Findings after inspection, including if nothing found. 
• Location car set out, if applicable 
Trains operating Line of Road will continue to report locomotive and car defects to the dispatcher for handling.  The 
dispatcher will notify the Mechanical Assistance Coordinator.   
 
3.4 Recording and Notification Inspection Results 
Complete Crew Information Form. 
 
Notify the appropriate personnel when cars are set out en route to make sure the car or cars are not moved before inspection or 
repairs are made. If car(s) must be set out at a repair point before train may continue, crew member must inform the train dispatcher 
or yardmaster of that fact. Person receiving report will notify Mechanical Department with Bad Order report.

Section 6 – Dimensional Equipment

Section 6 – Dimensional Equipment 
 
 
1.0 General  
Wherever the term “train” appears herein, it also applies to engines and transfers.  Wherever the term “protection notice” appears 
herein, it also applies to “blanket clearance.”  
 
1.1 Dimensional Shipment Standards  
A dimensional shipment is one, which exceeds the maximum standards of size, weight, and/or height of center of gravity as 
established by CPKC.  
 
CPKC defines dimensional traffic as being any shipment exceeding Plate F. 
 
 
 
Dimensional traffic may be easily identified by width, height, length.

sections.text:
2.0 Protection Notices  
A protection notice affords protection only upon Main Tracks, Sidings, Interchange Tracks, or other tracks specifically identified in 
the protection notice.  
 
2.1 Format of Protection Notices  
Format of the protection notice has been divided into 6 sections: 
 
“Section 1”:  Lists e-mail addresses which receive a copy.  Specifies the file number, the classification, and indicates if the 
shipment is governed by Specific Restrictions.  
• 
A file number commencing with “DL” indicates that General Restrictions apply (e.g., DL4011109).  
• 
A file number commencing with “RL” indicates General and Specific Restrictions apply (e.g., RL4013099).  
 
“Section 2”: Specifies the date the Protection Notice was issued. Specifies the characteristics of the shipment, including the car 
number(s), car marshaling, type of lading, shipper/origin, consignee/destination, full route, and CPKC routing.  
 
“Section 3”:  Specifies the measurements of the shipment:  height, width, length, gross weight, center of gravity from the truck 
center and the combined center of gravity.  
 
“Section 4”:  Specifies the subdivision name and the mileage points between which the protection notice applies on the 
subdivision. Specifies the W-code Classification.  
 
“Section 5”:  Specifies the “Specific Restrictions” that apply to a load at precise locations along its routing.  They are listed by 
mileage in the sequence in which they will be encountered.  Some examples are  reduce speed over bridges or passing specific 
obstructions; stop, examine, and proceed with crew observing the movement; and special marshaling.  
 
“Section 6”:  Specifies the “Code 6 Instruction message” and file number of the Protection Notice.  The “Code 6 Instruction 
message” on the train consist must be exactly as shown in Section 6 of the Protection Notice.  
 
2.2 Dimensional Traffic – Protection Notice Exceptions  
All dimensional traffic, with the following exceptions, must be protected by a protection notice:  
 
Piggyback flat cars loaded with truck trailers not exceeding 17’ 6” ATR (Above Top of Rail) by 8’ 6” wide.  This traffic can be 
handled without restriction.

sections.title: 2.3 Overloaded cars
sections.text:
2.3 Overloaded cars   
Unless otherwise indicated on train consist, overloaded cars may be accepted without additional authority. Overloaded cars which 
are NOT acceptable for movement without additional protection, will be identified as such on train consists and must be authorized 
by dimensional protection notice. 
 
2.4 Copy of Protection Notice  
A copy of the Protection Notice must:  
• 
accompany the movement from origin station to destination station,  
• 
be attached to the shipment’s waybill (if a waybill is provided).  
 
2.5 Information on Protection Notice  
The following information will be provided immediately after the addresses on each Protection Notice.  
Examples:  
• 
DL4011109 W-08 GENERAL RESTRICTIONS APPLY  
or  
• 
RL4013099 W-05-07 GENERAL AND SPECIFIC RESTRICTIONS APPLY  
a) File Number  
• 
A file number commencing with “DL” indicates that General Restrictions apply. (e.g. DL4011109)  
• 
A file number commencing with “RL” indicates General and Specific Restrictions apply. (e.g. RL4013099)  
b) Classification  
• 
W-08 indicates the classification of the shipment.  
• 
W-05-07 indicates the smallest and largest classification when the classification varies throughout the shipments 
entire route.  
c) Restrictions  
• 
“General Restrictions Apply,” indicates that subsection 4.0 applies.  
• 
“General and Specific Restrictions Apply,” indicates that SPECIFIC RESTRICTIONS of the protection notice also 
apply.  
 
2.6 The crew of a train or engine handling dimensional traffic  
Must comply with all applicable specific restrictions listed in the Protection Notice and are responsible to ensure dimensional 
traffic is not diverted from the limits stated in section 4 of the Protection Notice.  If necessary to move the shipment outside of 
these limits, a revised protection notice must be obtained.  
 
In terminals where crews are not in possession of Protection Notices, the person in charge is responsible to protect these limits. 
 
2.7  Diverting Dimensional Traffic from Limits under Section 4   
The crew of a train or engine handling dimensional traffic is responsible to ensure a dimensional shipment is not diverted from 
the limits stated in section 4 of the Protection Notice. If necessary to move the shipment in an area outside of these limits, a 
revised protection notice must be obtained. In terminals where crews are not in possession of Protection Notices, the yardmaster 
is responsible to protect these limits.

For overhanging shipments or shipments loaded on cars of 42 feet or longer, the “Effective Width” is reflected by a more restrictive 
classification.   
 
Note: Classification W-00 refers to dimensional traffic that has an effective width of 10’8” or less (e.g. shipment exceeds CP 
maximum weight or height standards but not maximum width standards).  
 
In the application of 4.2 (meet and passing), non-dimensional traffic shall be treated as being W-00. 
 
4.0 General Restrictions 
The following definitions apply in this subsection:  
 
Restricted Meet: When the train handling the wide traffic is required to move past trains, equipment, or other permissible wide 
traffic, movements must be stopped, and inspection made to ensure that adequate clearance exists before proceeding.  
Note:  A Restricted Meet is not required at the following location(s) where tracks are known to diverge onto separate roadbeds. 
 
Subdivision 
Location 
Watertown 
Between MP 95.36 at Juneau BLVD and MP 99.43 N. 
Brookfield RD NO 1 and NO 2 MT’s. 
 
Unrestricted Meet: Movements may meet or pass without restrictions.   
 
The meet and pass instructions listed herein are calculated on standard track centers between adjacent tracks on the same 
roadbed. Standard track centers are 13 feet between main tracks and 14 feet between a main track and a track other than a main 
track.  Some locations on CP have track centers that exceed these standards. At such locations where track centers between 
adjacent tracks on the same roadbed are known to exceed these standards, meet and pass instructions may be relaxed if a 
Restricted Meet takes place. 
 
4.1 Specific Meet/Pass Instructions  
Classification W-09 & W-10:   
• 
Due to extreme width, shipment to be moved in DAYLIGHT ONLY, unless otherwise authorized by the Superintendent 
– Field Operations.  
 
Trains handling W-09 or W-10 traffic must approach all track units prepared to stop unless it is determined that adequate clearance 
exists.  
 
Classification W-08 to W-10:    
Adjacent Main Tracks (Multiple main track Territory)  
• 
All adjacent main tracks to be kept clear of trains and equipment during movement.  
• 
Also: See item 4.3 for further restrictions applicable at SPECIFIC MILEAGES or SIDINGS where track centers are LESS 
than standard.  
 
4.2 Meet/Pass Instruction Charts  
These charts do not apply on the Northeast US East Region. See item 4.4.  
 
The Meet/Pass Instruction Charts 1 and 2 may be used to determine meet and pass restrictions.   
 
Some locations exist where track centers do not meet standard, refer to item 4.3 for exception locations and chart reference key.

sections.text:
5.0 Handling Procedures 
 
5.1 Permission in Train   
Before any dimensional traffic may be placed in a train, permission of the Chief of Train Dispatchers (COTD) must be secured.   
 
Conductor must confirm with Train Dispatcher/Operations Supervisor that authority has been granted for movement of a 
dimensional traffic before leaving their initial terminal or when picking up dimensional traffic enroute.  
 
Note: Train Dispatcher or Operations Supervisor will be responsible for notifying adjoining Train Dispatcher or Operations 
Supervisor territories for that train movement.  
 
Note: Permission will be withheld until appropriate NEXUS dimensional information has been updated.  
 
When requesting permission from the Train Dispatcher or Operations Supervisor, the employee doing so must supply the following 
information:  
• 
Car initials and number,  
• 
Classification (such as W-03, or W-03-07),  
• 
Specific Restrictions, if any,  
• 
Protection Notice file number,  
• 
Any other information that may be required.  
 
5.2 Setting out Dimensional Traffic  
Before setting out dimensional traffic (W-01 or greater), at locations where yardmasters cannot provide the necessary protection 
against other movement, the crew must obtain permission from the Train Dispatcher or Operations Supervisor. Conductor will 
notify the Train Dispatcher or Operations Supervisor the car initial and number and location of dimensional shipment. The Train 
Dispatcher or Operations Supervisor will then issue a track bulletin to approaching train movements if car is set out on an adjacent 
track next to a main track or controlled siding advising the location of the dimensional shipment and any instructions pertaining to 
the protection of such shipment. 
 
5.3 Protection of Moves  
Where Yardmasters or other employees in charge of movements are on duty to instruct moves, the Train Dispatcher or Operations 
Supervisor will notify them of the presence of dimensional shipment in a train before that train enters the yard under their 
jurisdiction.  The Yardmaster or other employee in charge of movements within these yards will be responsible to keep crews 
informed of the location of conflicting dimensional traffic within those yards, while on duty.  Train Dispatcher or Operations 
Supervisor will provide for protection against main track movements as outlined in Item 5.3.

sections.title: 5.4 Operating Through Yards, Sidings, Interchange Track and Within Yard Limits
sections.text:
5.4 Operating Through Yards, Sidings, Interchange Track and Within Yard Limits    
Crews must be especially watchful when operating through yards, sidings, interchange tracks and yard limits to ensure ample side 
clearance exists between dimensional traffic being handled and equipment on adjacent tracks.  
 
Crews must also ensure ample side clearance exists between equipment being handled and dimensional traffic on adjacent tracks.  
 
Where overhead or side clearance is doubtful, movement must be stopped, and inspection made to ensure that adequate 
clearance exists before proceeding.  
 
5.5 Marshaling of Dimensional Shipments  
Unless otherwise indicated in the car marshaling instruction of the protection notice, dimensional shipments may be marshaled 
without restriction. However, to permit visual observation by the crews, the dimensional shipments requiring a physical examination 
in order to clear a specific location, shall be marshaled as close as possible to the lead locomotive.  
 
On trains operating without a manned caboose, all dimensional traffic that would normally be marshaled to permit visual 
observation by the crew shall be marshaled as close as possible to, but not more than 2000 feet from the controlling unit.    
 
Note: Train consist, or protection notice will indicate dimensional shipments to which this item applies. 
 
5.6 Movement Past Other Traffic Adjacent Track  
When the dimensions of traffic do not permit unrestricted movement past other traffic on adjacent tracks and it is not practicable 
for the Train Dispatcher or Operations Supervisor to maintain blocking devices or to withhold operating authority, the Train 
Dispatcher or Operations Supervisor may use verbal  
instructions or issue a track bulletin to protect restricted meets against other main track movements.  
 
5.7 Joint Trackage   
Prior to a dimensional shipment being moved over joint trackage, permission must be obtain from the concerned railroad(s).  
 
5.8 Switching   
Dimensional shipments are not to be humped or kicked.

Section 7 – General Information 
 
CPKC Health Services 
CPKC’s Health Services (HS) Team supports Medical Fitness for Duty, Alcohol and Drug Free Workplace and Disability 
Management policies, procedures, and programs. CPKC employees are required to comply with these Policies and 
Procedures and requests made by the HS Team to support safe railway operations. Failure to comply with the policies, 
procedure or requests means HS is not able to determine an employee’s fitness for duty.  
 
Noncompliance with policies, procedures or requests may result in removal from service, investigation and disciplinary action 
including suspension without pay up to and including dismissal.  
 
Full details of the programs can be found on CPKC Station under Employees >> Health Services CPKC Health Services  
 
Medical Fitness for Duty 
Employees may require regulated and non-regulated medical assessments including Commercial Driver Medicals, Periodic 
Medical Assessments and Hearing and Vision exams. CPKC’s designated vendor for these assessments is WellPoint who 
is provided with a list of employees who require these exams. Employees who are due for their assessment can call or email 
WellPoint to schedule their appointment prior to their due date using the contact details below. WellPoint will verify the 
individual’s name from the list or will follow up with CPKC’s Health Services if the employee is not on the list. Medical exams 
are scheduled at the clinic closest to individual’s location. 
Contact Information:   
WellPoint Health Ltd.   
Phone: 1-833-797-4663   
Email: intake@wellpoint.ca  
Alcohol and Drug Programs 
CPKC is committed to protecting the safety, health and well-being of all employees, other individuals in our workplace, and 
the general public. We recognize that alcohol and drug use pose a significant threat to these goals. We have established 
programs that balance our respect for individuals with the need to maintain an alcohol and drug-free work environment. 
Should you have any questions or concerns regarding CPKC’s Drug and Alcohol Program or Policies, please 
contact Manager Drug and Alcohol Programs / DER. at 612-209-8444 or CP_DER@cpr.ca 
 
Disability Management 
The Disability Management Program supports employee health and well-being by promoting early intervention to employees 
who become ill or injured and facilitating timely and safe return to work, including reintegration to regular or modified/alternate 
work duties as appropriate.  
 
Employee Assistance Program (EAP)  
In addition, CPKC offers all employees access to EAP which provides you and your dependents with immediate and 
confidential help for any work, health or life concern.  You can contact the EAP by calling their call center or visiting the 
website below:   
 
1-833-594-0869 or visit one.telushealth.com (Username: CPKC Password: eap) 
 
You can also download the “TELUS Health One” app at your device app store.
